liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Baba O'Riley** (2 reviews): Reviewer loved the encore pairing of this song going into Tomorrow Never Knows; Listed by the reviewer as a highlight, together with Tomorrow Never Knows [8][19]
- **West L.A. Fadeaway** (1 review): Jerry hands Vince solo room but Vince holds back; Jerry then returns at the bridge and plays forcefully [12]
- **Candyman** (1 review): Reviewer can't get enough of this performance, and says Jerry played at top form [11]
- **Liberty** (1 review): Reviewer says it was the only time they saw the same song in consecutive shows, across different cities [16]
- **Samson And Delilah** (1 review): The wedding party was seated up front and had its first dance to this song [13]
- **Broken Arrow** (1 review): Listed by the reviewer as a highlight of the show [19]
- **He's Gone** (1 review): Reviewer praises the vocal jam in this song as a standout [8]
- **Tomorrow Never Knows** (1 review): Reviewer says the band always played this song well, and this version is no exception [18]

## Setlist highlights

- **Baba O'Riley**: rare: 12 archived performances [20]
- **Tomorrow Never Knows**: rare: 12 archived performances [20]

## The recordings

- **gd1993-03-21.151664.sbd.cm.miller.t.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 153 min [1]
- **gd93-03-21.ST250.georges.7470.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 20 songs; 159 min; rated 4.25/5 by 4 [3]. Said about its sound: Audience recording sounds very good apart from some audience chatter; Reviewer finds the audience recording mono-sounding but says EQ software can improve it; Reviewer calls the audience recording very good with some chatter, and disputes that it sounds monaural [11][14][15]
- **gd93-03-21.sbd.miller.28429.sbeok.flacf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 150 min; rated 3.08/5 by 12 [6]
- **gd1993-03-21.151159.sbd.miller.flac2448**: soundboard; 20 songs; 153 min [2]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says the Omni's acoustics were superb in the room, though that doesn't come through on recordings; the building was later demolished [8]
- A wedding took place on the Omni floor during the set break; the band waited for the couple's kiss [13]
- Reviewer rates this the best show of the Spring 1993 run they have heard [9]
- Reviewer says first sets on this tour were typically strong, and they attended all three Omni nights [11]
- Reviewer finds set one promising but set two labored, leaning heavily on newer songs and failing to take off [15]
- Reviewer felt some of the newer songs lacked punch and the band's enthusiasm seemed to be fading [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1993-03-21.151664.sbd.cm.miller.t.flac16**: taped by Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  December 11, 2020; source: SBD > DAT Master (48k) > Cassette Master (Tascam 122mkIII/TDK SA-X100) [1]
- **gd93-03-21.ST250.georges.7470.sbeok.shnf**: taped by James Young and Ron Kaiser; transferred by Nick Georges; source: Audience: Soundfield ST-250's [3]. Also: Recorded with a Soundfield ST-250 into a Sony D10 Pro-II at 48k, master DAT, taped by James Young and Ron Kaiser [3]
- **gd93-03-21.sbd.miller.28429.sbeok.flacf**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD> Dat> Cassette Master> Dat> CD> EAC> SHN> WAV> Samplitude Professional v8.0> FLAC; Edited By Charlie Miller [6]
- **gd1993-03-21.151159.sbd.miller.flac2448**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  December 11, 2020; source: SBD > DAT Master (48k) > Cassette Master (Tascam 122mkIII/TDK SA-X100) [2]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Sameh Tawfik Grateful Dead: [1993-03-21 The Omni, Atlanta, GA, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1993-03-21-the-omni-atlanta-ga-usa/) [21]
